publications.title: Probabilistic robustness for compressor controls in transient pipeline networks
publications.abstract:
Abstract
                  Uncertainty plays a crucial role in modeling and optimization of complex systems across various applications. In this paper, uncertain gas transport through pipeline networks is considered and a novel strategy to measure the robustness of deterministically computed compressor and valve controls, the probabilistic robustness, is presented. Initially, an optimal control for a deterministic gas network problem is computed such that the total control cost is minimized with respect to box constraints for the pressure. Subsequently, the model is perturbed by uncertain gas demands. The probability, that the uncertain gas pressures- based on the a priori deterministic optimal control- satisfy the box constraints, is evaluated. Moreover, buffer zones are introduced in order to tighten the pressure bounds in the deterministic scenario. Optimal controls for the deterministic scenario with buffer zones are also applied to the uncertain scenario, allowing to analyze the impact of the buffer zones on the probabilistic robustness of the optimal controls. For the computation of the probability, we apply a kernel density estimator based on samples of the uncertain pressure at chosen locations. In order to reduce the computational effort of generating the samples, we combine the kernel density estimator approach with a stochastic collocation method which approximates the pressure at the chosen locations in the stochastic space. Finally, we discuss generalizations of the probabilistic robustness check and we present numerical results for a gas network taken from the public gas library.

publications.title: pubchem-mcp-server
publications.abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for the PubChem chemical database, providing compound search (name, SMILES, InChIKey, formula, substructure, 2D similarity), physicochemical and pharmacological properties, GHS safety data, bioactivity profiles, cross-references, and entity summaries for assays, genes, proteins, and taxa.

publications.title: mdcx: verified conversion of document collections to queryable Markdown
publications.abstract: Converts complete document collections to Markdown, checking each file against the text the original actually exposes, packages the resulting corpus with its index and provenance into a single encrypted file, and exposes it to agents through the Model Context Protocol. Over a collection of 99 documents, answering one query through the package costs 435 model tokens against the 2,265,488 required to read the originals.
publications.source_detail: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

publications.title: RearAccess.com: An Independently Maintained Access Guide to NARA Record Group 615 (Project Blue Book and Related UAP Records)
publications.abstract: RearAccess.com (https://rearaccess.com/) is an independent, non-governmental research site that mirrors and indexes the U.S. National Archives' Record Group 615 bulk releases relating to Project Blue Book (1947-1969) and later Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) record transfers. The underlying archival records are U.S. federal public-domain material; the site's contribution is a parsed, searchable index and finding aids across 10,743 archival descriptions, 117,168 digital objects, and 10,276 individual Project Blue Book case files, indexed by U.S. state/territory and by year (1947-1969), plus 375 additional unsealed federal records and 122 sub-collections spanning textual/microfilm records, still photographs, moving images and sound, presidential library correspondence, and born-digital electronic records. Notably, the busiest single month across the full case-file run is November 1957 (364 files), not the famous "flap" of summer 1952, and roughly 480 case files describe sightings over open water identified only by latitude/longitude. This upload is a short access guide/finding aid summarizing that index and its methodology for researchers, with links to the case-file index, collections overview, and bulk dataset export. RearAccess.com is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, NARA or any government agency.
publications.source_detail: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

publications.title: Deliberate: An open-source Python toolkit for AI-assisted public deliberation analysis
publications.abstract: Public deliberation platforms generate large volumes of unstructured citizen contributions requiring systematic analysis to support evidence-based policymaking. Existing solutions typically offer isolated functionalities, lacking integrated workflows that transform raw text into structured analytical outputs. This paper presents DELIBERATE, an open-source Python toolkit for AI-assisted deliberation analysis. It provides three composable services: Trend Discovery, which clusters contributions using unsupervised learning and LLM-based semantic enrichment; Argument Analysis, which performs argumentation mining and argument classification; and Content Quality, which automates content moderation by identifying unsuitable contributions. DELIBERATE produces structured outputs for downstream policy analysis and supports reproducible experimentation.

publications.title: OpenBrowse: Self-hosted AI browser agents
publications.abstract: OpenBrowse is an open-source, self-hosted alternative to Browser Use Cloud: AI browser agents that run on your own hardware, driven through the v3 REST API, with schema-validated structured output, anti-hallucination grounding guards, and a live visual dashboard.
